notes.title: More focused battle encounters - Devlog #7
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/6ee54a8b59208bb9e96834ef01f9e1d5053371c1.gif
How could this broken shell of a man, barely able to carry the weight of his own sword, be the Burning Terror which drove me to hide here? He seemed to have Demons of his own, that he struggled to contain... and he was losing.

Changes to the battle system
We’ve made a complete overhaul of Crawlyard's battle encounters. Before, it felt like a hybrid of Vampire Survivors and Loop Hero, but now it’s more like Hadean Tactics. What I mean by that is that each encounter now has its own battle zone, borders and enemies, all happening within the stage of your chosen performance. 

Basically, we aimed to arrive at a seamless transition between exploration and skirmish like you'd see in modern JRPGs. Each battle is a pretty much consistent experience and enemies won’t spawn totally randomly (well, there's still a hint of randomness within specific conditions). Here, a fancy gif where I'm using battle brushes to create a zone for the next battle encounter.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/77d27085b7ef5cbe69a773e03473a130378af6ed.gif
Mapping out a death zone in sleepy dorms

Encounter system
So I was talking about randomness, right? Well, our encounters aren’t exactly fixed - each time you visit  a stage and engage in one of its battles, there's a tiny invisible counter that goes up by one. The higher the value of that counter is, the more new random enemies we add to this encounter's list, until it reaches a pretty round number like 10 or 100, and then you’ll have such a wide roster of enemies that it might indeed seem random (but not totally random still).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/fc11693250dd4636c83009a1cad7120b7e2111d7.png

Better yet, each encounter adapts to your class, level and build. Even if you make a Knight build that's really good for dueling single foes, I will make sure that at some point a hoard of lesser enemies with a poison attribute will spawn at once, and you’ll have to improvise, adapt and overcome.
So, no steamrolling dungeons with a meta build, but I promise you WILL have a good time [strike]you little munchkin bastards[/strike].

Is it a roguelike already?
I like to have some kind of adaptive randomness. Things need to be spicy and interesting with you guys, because once you figure out a winning strategy you’ll get bored with the game. Making the game adapt to current circumstances is a good way to keep you engaged (and die, a lot, which I like, a lot). 

And as much as I would love to just delegate every decision to some randomizing algorithm, I can't deny the pleasure or torturing you guys. Thinking about you suffering in those encounters is a thing that keeps me alive and motivated, which is what you want from your favourite developer.

[hr][/hr]
Should I talk about the new navigation system in the next devlog? Or about our roguelite progression? Or both? Let me know in the comments or nudge me in Crawlyard Discord.
 
Anyways, wait for the new demo for Steam Next Fest: October Edition - we will be there.

Until next time, your one and only
Vovun-Bubblegum, game designer.

notes.title: Something to perk you up
notes.content:
Yo everyone, it’s time to share another big change we work on right now for the game. Enter the PERKS. Capital letters only for the bigger impression.

So what is a perk in Crawlyard?
Well, I assume you all know what the general idea of perk is, but in general, now you acquire action points (basically this is exp, but we wanted to be fancy) and spend it on perks. What can they do?
Everything!
Mostly they give you new cards, cause I want to ditch the bored to death “get 1 of 3 cards after each battle” mechanic. But they also can give you passive abilities (i.e. you deal fire attacks on low HP or get bonus armor for each point of damage you get). They also can change cards behavior, and even remove and upgrade cards in your deck. They can give you items, and change the gameplay mechanics in general. And we’re going to unleash our internal creative demons designing the perks.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/8cbb404ad190a6d387b976a840a431e13a5eacb6.png

And how interesting perks are going to be?
Well, it depends. We want them to be your general progress meter and make your puppet grow with time spent in the dungeons. Perks will replace attribute growth, so perks can also raise your stats, like health, damage, speed, etc.
For now, we are only sure about the general outline and possibilities the perks can give you. We throw in ideas about it, but it’s more about testing and figuring out the best ones. And also don’t forget about balancing all of that to keep the gameplay fun and hardcore - you should get more powerful with perks but not too much, or else challenges you face will become too hollow and dull.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/8f7f99966e5d3acf522ef7d6b03286226e2a8769.png

So wait, now you upgrade perks now instead of stats?
Yeah, that’s what we’re going to implement. It just sounded like a good idea and I had no arguments with myself why we shouldn’t do it.
But still, it’s not the only thing that will interact with your cards/abilities. We will also showcase a character that can upgrade cards in two different ways, and also a bit later I’ll tell you about “dark cards” that bosses use against you… but it’s a story for another time.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/776e89b66f6b0acd87d4ab1e68e91e542cb5399b.png

notes.title: Big changes vol. 1: Performances
notes.content:
Hey guys, it’s time to share the big changes we are working on right now for the game. Without further interruption, let me tell you about our Performances.

What?
Performances will replace the rooms and affectors system we have currently. Before, you had a straightforward floor layout that contained battle rooms and empty spaces for you to place the affector cards onto. Now, we decided to merge them together, creating the ultimate beast - a proper theatrical performance.

It works like this: in the beginning you have a floor with only a starting room and a boss room, and a number of free slots between them (usually, the deeper you go the more slots there will be). You draw performances into your hand just like you did with affectors, and you can place them on the floor map according to your battle strategy or quest requirements. The layout's structure is also non-linear now, which means at some point you can choose between several performances to go to.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/276b6dfdd761a32647cc755e11e005f8cd6055f2.png

Okay, but why?
When we claimed that you can build your own dungeon in the game, just putting 2-3 rooms inside a predetermined pattern doesn’t sound that impressive. Having you physically assemble the majority of the dungeon? Now that sounds like a fancy feature! 
Mechanically it doesn’t change the flow of the game much – each performance still has battles, enemies, and special modifiers that twist the rules of the game. But we also wanted to highlight the game's narrative potential, fixing the disjointed experience of breezing through dozens of generic rooms randomly slapped together. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/965cfd449922a2d1dafec13a07097b7fccf052d2.png

Gimme more
Okay, so let’s break it down in a bit more detail:

 Each performance contains a set of 3-6 encounters with enemies unique for this biome, or even created specifically for this particular story.
 Each performance is a small story in itself, exactly like a real theatrical play. It expands on the world of the game without unnecessary walls of text, relying heavily on environmental and mechanical design, and may sometimes include the characters you meet in the Mansion.
 Each performance has a set of unique conditions that change the game’s rules to some extent. Imagine a performance about escaping from a dilapidated temple, where each reward makes you slower and your risk falling into the abyss together with the crumbling floor, or a performance where previously defeated enemies haunt you as ghosts.
 Each performance has its own set of mini-quests and conditions that, if completed, provide you with extra rewards.

And did I mention that all of them are visually distinct and contain a set of unique graphics, lighting, and visual effects?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/8cb3c1e9952a920d1b3edc0fc29c310eea549a56.png

So these are performances in a nutshell. Check out the next devlog for more information about upcoming changes and inner workings of the development process!

notes.title: Crawlyard DevBlog #4
notes.content:
Hey guys, long time no see! Sorry for the long delay between posts, these months were pretty challenging for the development and we had no time to spare.

That only means that the game’s becoming even better than it was. Now, for the updates.

Stances passive effects
Remember the Knight puppet having different stances tied to the main stats? Well, guess what – they now have passive effects that work when you activate a specific stance.

 Shield stance - blocks one attack per 3 (or maybe 4? not sure) seconds. In the future, we might rework ability cards in a way that will further reduce the blocking cooldown, allowing you to potentially negate EVERYTHING that comes at you.
 Spear stance - gives you bonus damage based on your speed. That doesn’t really sound that impressive, but hear me out - it also accelerates you while you’re moving. So your first attack will basically be a charge that sometimes one-shots enemies (the feebler ones, anyway). It should also have a good synergy with Break Distance and Charge abilities, since they affect your mobility on the battlefield.
 Sword stance - deals splash damage to surrounding enemies and boosts your damage based on missing health. So positioning yourself right in the heart of the battle and always being on the brink of death is a winning strategy for this stance. Not ready yet, but will be added soon.

https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/40852172/05cda231f8bb47927f38b18e0266c404efa34e17.png

In-run progression
As you probably already noticed, we’ve added a progression system within the dungeon run. You develop your stats and get new cards that are generally tied to their respective stats. The Pulse cards will be implemented later as they have special mechanics.

https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/40852172/11059aefa58679572174c12625261e0daf8b9225.png

And as for progression between runs, aside from the fact that you unlock new NPCs of course, we have quite the pool of options to test and find out what suits the game most of all. "Cross-run" progression will be a part of what we call the "Big Changes" list we'll be presenting to our publisher. Which leads us to...

The publisher
So we figured that in order to elevate Crawlyard to a different level and keep making games after that, we’d need financial and marketing support from a publisher. And we found one, or should I say  they found us. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/e27e20feb548c8703c17bedcdbf17ee05a7be80e.png

We will be partnering with Crunching Koalas to update visuals of the game, deepen the gameplay, create more characters and flesh out their stories, and also implement all those numerous features we had to painfully archive before. We'll probably move the release date further, but not too much. Besides, having stable salaries will help us avoid relying on Early Access, so we will be able to actually deliver the full game earlier than we initially planned.

Afterword
That will be all for today. Keep an eye out for other devlogs – we might drop another one soon where we explore the ways to bring our characters to life, and maybe one more dedicated to the game's visual design. And then we'll finally be able to share the Big Chances with you, and the pipeline for improving the game, widening its scope and polishing it further.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/dd63a3f4360cbde6ecc174e16b92ecedef419df6.png

Your regular "horny and depressed" indie game developer, signing out.

notes.title: Crawlyard Demo is out!
notes.content:
Welcome to Crawlyard Devlogs! Steam Next Fest is upon us, and this time we have a bit more to show you than screenshots and gifs and sketches. The story prologue is here, and you can download it for free to check out a fraction of what our full game will be able to offer!
We will keep polishing the demo and implementing some of the non-crucial changes and fixes in real time, so by the end of Fest the game will definitely become even better.

Welcome, Inspector
You arrive at the Mansion slightly ahead of schedule. Nobody greets you, and nobody guides you, yet the Mansion still opens up to you somewhat, both figuratively and literally. Your resources are limited, other residents don't quite know what to make of you, and from the meta-narrative perspective, your future is pretty much determined...
But would you still like to walk this path with us?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/ce5653a41acdac99a5c55ece3ca57b50b4d3c79c.png

The prologue is not essential for you to understand the main story, far from it. But you will be able to look behind the scenes just a few weeks prior to the start of the grand performance, and get to know some of the characters in advance. 
Gameplay-wise, the demo shows off less than a quarter of cards, systems and activities you will be able to enjoy in the full game, so it's just an appetizer to the main dish.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/dd06f684ec9fc599740d6f5a06dff0d4a58a5fe0.png


Community and Feedback
The demo will be further polished based on the feedback we get – there's no better opportunity to get actual, genuine playtests than now, so we can correct problematic aspects of the game before they take root. We will be closely monitoring our players' impressions, and for this purpose we're launching our official public Discord server!
Just click on the picture to join the server. Hopefully, one day it will become full of life, memes and embarrassing bug reports just like you'd expect.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/c0b4900a75a949401c7cbe2aa9be46dc22c0e87c.png

Our ridiculously charismatic game designer has also been doing lots of marketing and publicity work behind the scenes, and we actually managed to get a Golden Ticket after an intense pitch battle during the Digital Dragons Acceleration Programme! Still up to debate if we should take them up on their publishing offer or not, but that sure was a huge confidence boost. 


Afterword
There's a lot to do still, but this was an incredibly important milestone. The demo serves as a tiny glimpse into the full game, and what's even more important, it shows that the backbone of the project works. All that's left is adding more content, polishing the existing mechanics, and introducing some cheeky narrative tricks to make the story truly shine. Stay tuned, we've only just begun!
Exhausted yet happy PR person, signing out.

notes.title: Crawlyard DevBlog #3
notes.content:
Welcome to Crawlyard Devlogs! We've been busy preparing for Gamescom, polishing the demo, upgrading the graphics, and implementing new systems. The game evolved immensely since we've last got in contact with the community, we've added a new trailer, updated the game page, started working with voice actors, and so much more.

There were lots of themes for a devlog to choose from, but we decided to focus on our beloved puppets for once. Please meet the Knight – your tireless warrior, valiant protector, and the most trusty explorer of the backstage.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/2a3b2b0395d9ebe8992deab3916a197e267c8094.png


Stances
The Knight rushes straight into battle and is able to soak up a lot of damage. Sounds familiar? Oh, we'll have our fair share of interesting game design decisions, from double stat system to physically replacing parts of your dolls to change its abilities, but we all agreed that the core concept should be simple enough to understand intuitively.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/98021a8a738e5c3bcc455be3d884ec04e1930d4c.gif

But even on the most basic level you can manipulate the way your Knight advances with the help of his unique class feature: battle stances. Switching between them mid-fight allows your knight to swiftly go from offense to defense if things aren't looking too great, or choose a more tactical approach for a particularly tricky enemy.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/145962b2a556c8957bb75445c196f17406f5db54.gif


Abilities
But, as much as we like our brave little explorers, you probably shouldn't expect much ingenuity from a puppet. Thankfully, Crawlyard is far from being an idle game, so you can, and probably should, always use abilities to lend your Knight a hand in battle. This is where both the strategic deck building and tactical ability juggling come into play.

There are so many more abilities we still aim to implement to make playing as a "straightforward" Knight fun, challenging and satisfying on every level! Of course it will require a lot of game design and testing effort, but we believe it will be totally worth it in the end.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/9cdff36a95f4a550b660ef6c26dec75d8728d2e2.gif


Truth to be told, we were at first thinking of making more dolls with unique class cards, but eventually decided to focus our efforts on polishing the archetypes embodying all those other individual cases. After all, puppets get repurposed to play different roles all the time. 

So, who will your Knight become? A raging berserk? A stalwart paladin? A nimble fencer? A flashy magical warrior? Or, maybe, a universalist cherry-picking the best individual abilities but never quite reaching the level of the specialists' earth-shattering combos? As always, feel free to experiment and choose something that suits you the most.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/dd9569adf827ab50dbf1d39dd19f6e689fb9494a.png


Afterword
And that concludes our short sneak peek into the class system. Other doll types will have a vastly unique way to play them which would once again be further diversified by their specific mechanics and decks, but that's a story for another time. Make sure to stay tuned!
Your regular "huh, so I'll be doing design now, too?" indie game developer, signing out.

notes.title: Crawlyard DevBlog #2
notes.content:
Welcome to Crawlyard Devlogs! These weeks have been extremely busy for us, but we managed to make plenty of powerful changes, introduce new concepts to the gameplay, work on UI and story (enough to dedicate an entire update to each!) and now steadily continue to add more material to the game.


Room layout
Certain actions often become a chore after a few hours of repetition. So our tech guys decided to work on the game flow a bit and cut on unnecessary hustle. Here's what it looked like before, when you had to drag every room card one after another to determine your run's layout:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/f08b7c6477bb5fa6183455366b1c555ee23eab7d.png

And here's how we decided to change it. Some "filler" rooms are now randomly fixed in place, and you can modify them with actual "affectors" –  cards that make all these intricate combos work. The player will still have plenty of strategical and tactical freedom in how they build the scene, now with fewer monotonous actions.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/4b9629dff52bff1afae8f3c71c8f7e3e7982c8da.png


Preparation stage
There's also a new preparation stage before each room cluster where you can pick your active hero, manage your deck and customize items. It will take a couple more tests to determine the optimal length of animations and other graphical flourishes so this stage is both concise yet striking, but the core concept is working nicely.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/abe2031b089087368da25f74157b33403f0b57a7.gif


New rooms
Our Mansion had hosted countless performances in the past, until it became able to mix and match different scenes on its own. Even within certain themes, or "biomes", there will be plenty of room variations for you to rest your eyes on. Here's less than 10% of the rooms you will see in the demo alone, and the whole game will have even more to offer!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/8fa44f45a5581e695d8e786c473aa6d814a672d5.gif
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/abec6e77bd735d29bc9352f25b47a6693a9fabba.gif


Afterword
And that's all for this update. Our sight is firmly fixed on our next important milestone: Steam Next Fest, an event celebrating indie games all over the world. The demo will be ready quite some time before it, but it just gives us extra weeks of tuning and polishing so our game can truly shine alongside all other gems. Good luck, and see you soon!
Your local newsperson, signing out.

notes.title: Crawlyard DevBlog #1
notes.content:
Welcome to Crawlyard Devlogs! We are steadily working on the game every single day, and we feel like sharing our creative process might prove to be interesting to our players and fellow developers alike. So, aside from posting progress reports and important public announcements, we'd also like to give you a glimpse into the world behind the stage.

Pretty fitting for a game that takes place in theatre, isn't it~


Early character designs
Our Mansion attracts unusual people, but for their quirks to truly stand out they have to be offset by more or less regular characters, too. At the beginning, the proportion of "normal" to "abnormal" was roughly 1:1, but the deeper we dive into it, the weirder our designs become.

We spent quite some time figuring out the best art style that wouldn't collide with our 3d visuals while being competent enough to stand on its own, attract attention and tell a story just as well as pages upon pages of text could. So until we reveal our finalized versions in due time, please check these earlier sketches out.


Barmaid
The Barmaid is meant to be a strong and confident woman – not without her share of peculiar worries, of course, or she wouldn't have ended up in the Mansion. She looks good both in traditional feminine and unisеx clothing, too, and we considered experimenting with exotic accessories and tattoos at one point as well. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/2e5d320c766b26f9520da82545897539a71694a2.png

Still, she is firmly placed on the "normal" side of our cast, so going for more familiar shapes and textures proved to be a better choice. This sketch list is already much closer to what we'll see in the end – just a few stylistic touches, and we're good.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/508b886f678bfed58f9bc9280774cdd1bb92a1b8.png


Puppeteer 
But if there is one single character who represents the "abnormal" side the best, it would be the Puppeteer. A person so mysterious their gender, race and even humanity are a tough puzzle to solve, we can clearly tell our artists had a lot of fun coming up with striking silhouettes and memorable visual details.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/fa4fc3699def508441d1f6792cba562e0081ccfb.png

The Puppeteer is all about their love for dolls and masks – to the point where they consider a doll transformation for themselves, too. Just you wait until you discover the way they emote when their face is hidden securely behind an elaborate mask!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40852172/3015352158d974ec76986506c75e602772d9b1ed.png


Afterword
That's it for now! We will be back with another blog pretty soon – there are some UI updates and really cool visual effects almost ready to be presented to the public. Thank you for following our game, and see you soon!
Scriptwriter, signing out.


Meanwhile, you can check additional updates on our SNS:
